passage:
"Saurabh, you missed your bus for me last night."
"There's another at eight. It's fine."
"It isn't nothing. You spent two hours on my charts." Sonali held out her notes. "Thank you. I can't fix your slides, but I can take the notes for Thursday's session, and I'll bring chai."
Saurabh scratched his ear. "You don't have to."
"I want to. Yesterday I nearly gave up on the whole chart section, and then you sat down and asked me one question at a time until it made sense. And next week, tell me what you're stuck on. I mean it. 🙏"
"Okay. Chai with less sugar, then."
"Done."

qa.q: How long did Saurabh spend on Sonali's charts?
qa.a: Saurabh spent two hours on Sonali's charts.

qa.q: Why does Sonali insist that it isn't nothing?
qa.a: Sonali feels deeply grateful, because Saurabh missed his bus and spent two hours on her charts, and she wants him to know it mattered.

qa.q: How does Sonali give something back?
qa.a: She offers to take the notes for Thursday's session, bring chai and help when Saurabh is stuck next week.

qa.q: How might Saurabh feel about Sonali's thanks?
qa.a: Saurabh scratches his ear and says she doesn't have to, which suggests he is a little shy but pleased.

grounding: A groupmate stayed late to help; the receiver thanks them and offers help in return.

passage:
Lab instructor's note, electronics lab, 14 November
On Tuesday evening I stayed to lock up and saw Payal still at Kishore's bench at 8 p.m., two hours after her own circuit was done. His amplifier kept failing, and his group's demo was the next morning. She traced the fault with him, step by step, to a reversed diode.
This morning, before the demo, I noticed Kishore leave a packet of her favourite chikki on her bench with a note. At the demo, when I asked who had debugged the amplifier, he said, "Payal helped me find the diode. I wouldn't have got it without her."
Later I heard him offer to go through her lab record with her before the viva, since he is strong on theory.
I have made a note to mention peer help in the course feedback.

qa.q: What fault did Payal help Kishore find?
How did Kishore seem to feel about Payal's help?
qa.a: Grateful, which he showed with chikki and a note, public credit and an offer of help in return.

qa.q: How did Kishore avoid taking the help for granted?
qa.a: He thanked her with a gift and note, credited her at the demo, and offered to go through her lab record before the viva.

qa.q: How might Payal feel when Kishore credits her at the demo?
qa.a: Appreciated and seen for staying late to help.

grounding: Shows a groupmate staying late to help, and responding with thanks and an offer of help in return rather than taking it for granted.

passage:
Wednesday
Maria stayed with me in the design studio till 11 last night, helping me fix the model that collapsed. She had her own jury today. She didn't even mention it till we were walking back to the hostel.
This morning I nearly just said "thanks yaar" and moved on, like always. That's the version of me that let people help and then forgot.
So instead I left chai and a note on her desk: "You saved my project and probably my sanity. Thank you." And after her jury I asked what she still needed. She said the presentation boards were a mess. I spent two hours after dinner cutting and mounting them with her.
She said I didn't have to. I said I know. That's the point.
Tonight she sent me a photo of the boards pinned up, with a heart drawn in the corner. Going to sleep feeling like a slightly better friend.
— Salma

qa.q: Till what time did Maria stay in the studio?
How does Salma feel going to sleep?
qa.a: Grateful and quietly proud, like a slightly better friend.

qa.q: How did Salma return Maria's help?
qa.a: With chai and a thank-you note, then two hours after dinner mounting Maria's presentation boards.

qa.q: How might Maria feel about Salma's help with the boards?
qa.a: Touched and appreciated, which she shows by sending a photo with a heart in the corner.

grounding: Illustrates being helped late at night by a groupmate and thanking her and helping in return instead of taking it for granted.
